name: Dr. CYJ Hair Filler

card.summary: A Korean scalp mesotherapy product combining hyaluronic acid and peptides, injected into the scalp by clinics with the aim of supporting hair-follicle health and fuller-looking hair.
card.note: Professional injectable; claims come from the manufacturer and retailers.

quick.overview:
Dr. CYJ Hair Filler is a mesotherapy product made by Caregen of South Korea. It combines hyaluronic acid with a complex of seven peptides and is marketed for scalp damaged by aging, stress, UV, dyes and chemical treatments.

The aim is a healthier scalp and follicles, which proponents link to better-looking hair. Retail pages cite no clinical studies.
quick.how: It is delivered by a trained professional as superficial injections into the scalp, usually as a series of sessions. People may combine it with other hair-loss treatments.
quick.risks: Any scalp injection carries risks such as pain, bruising, swelling and infection. Descriptions of the hyaluronic acid vary between sellers, and the product claims have not been tested in published trials.

lead: Dr. CYJ Hair Filler is a scalp mesotherapy product from Caregen Co., Ltd, a Seoul-based pharmaceutical company founded in 2001. Retail descriptions say it combines reticulated hyaluronic acid with seven peptides: Decapeptide-18, Oligopeptide-54, Decapeptide-10, Octapeptide-2, Octapeptide-11, Oligopeptide-71 and Decapeptide-28. [1]

It is sold as 2 x 1 ml and described as intradermal scalp injection, performed only by a trained professional. Its marketing says it addresses scalp damage from aging, stress, UV exposure, dyes, chemicals, braiding and transplants, supporting follicles and hair growth. [1]
These are manufacturer and retailer claims; the product page cites no clinical studies. [1]

chain: HA and peptides placed in the scalp dermis
Claimed support for scalp skin and follicles
angle.text: Users hope that delivering hyaluronic acid and peptides into the scalp improves follicle health and hair appearance. The benefit is claimed by the maker rather than demonstrated in published trials.

paras: The product page describes it as a medical hair filler for damaged scalp, injected superficially to mid-dermis by certified professionals. [1]
